notes.house: mu = 1.1 + 0.95*lean + 4.6*inc + E (lean = 2 x Cook PVI 2026), fundraising: + 1.25 x log(D / R individual contributions through June 30, $10k floor) - out of sample it cut competitive-seat error 5.5 % (2018) and 3.8 % (2022), and moves incumbency from 4.6 to 3.5; race polls from the state pages blended by precision (per-poll sd 5.6, shared 4.3; a poll's precision fades with a 63-day half-life, no hard window); seats with no Democrat or no Republican on the ballot are decided (CA-40 R-v-R, D-v-D top-two), an independent incumbent facing only a Democrat (CA-6) keeps incumbency; every race poll (House and Senate) is corrected for its pollster's measured lean (538's 2016-22 record, shrunk) or, failing that, its sponsor tag: D-sponsored polls ran 4.3 too Democratic and R-sponsored 4.1 too Republican against the non-partisan polls of the same race (1998-2022, same sign every cycle), and count at 0.58 weight; polls with more than 12 % undecided carry up to 26 % more error, a third candidate at 10 %+ 27 % more; LV and RV race polls are not adjusted (94 % of late race polls are LV; the generic-ballot fit carries LV/RV/adult offsets); Hispanic/Asian swing since 2024: + 12 x centred Hispanic CVAP share (Cubans at 0.25) + 11 x centred Asian share, before the poll blend (2025 NJ/VA governor and CA Prop 50 reversed the 2020-24 shift fully, specials did not; centred so the national environment is unchanged); every race poll is also corrected for its STATE's persistent polling miss (0.24 x the 2024 miss + 0.13 x 2022's, net of the national miss; out of sample -2.7 % Senate / -0.9 % House log loss); the demographic factors are UPDATED from the district polls (Bayesian, no tuned parameters: 2022 House log loss -5.1 %); heating-oil adjustment (judgment, not backtested): fuel-oil household share x retail heating-oil rise (Maine $5.91 now v $3.36 a year ago) x 650 gal x 1.04 pts per $1,000 x the share not yet in polls, against the president's party (Maine +0.6); errors t5: national 4.5 (shared with the Senate and governor draw), state 2.5, urban 2, Hispanic / Cuban / Asian group factors 15 per unit share, residual 5
notes.senate: mu = 1.4 + 0.80*E + 0.76*lean + 10.4*inc, prior sd 13.4 (refit on 326 races 2006-2024), polls from the Wikipedia race pages (per-poll sd 4.2, shared 4 - midterm x0.8); only polls of the candidates actually on the ballot, full field where a third candidate polls 10 %+; the margin is the main challenger minus the Republican - an independent where no Democrat is on the ballot (NE, ID, SD) or the independent leads the Democrat (MT). Independent wins are not counted as Democratic seats. A FUNDED independent with no Democrat on the ballot (>= $1M and >= 25 % of the Republican's June 30 money) gets the prior +12 with sd 9: the three famous successes (Orman +21, McMullin +21, Osborn +25 against the prior) are a selected sample - the unfunded independents of the same class ran -4 (Harrington 2020), -44 (O'Hara 2002) and -53 (Spannaus 1990), so the shift is gated on money and shrunk for three precedents. An unfunded independent (ID, SD in 2026) gets the plain prior, widened; with a Democrat also running (MT) the prior is widened x2; Hispanic/Asian swing term as in the House (12 x centred Hispanic CVAP share, Cubans at 0.25, 11 x Asian; state shares vs national), mean and group shocks both damped by the Senate's national slope 0.8; race polls corrected for the state's persistent polling miss (as the House) and for the white non-college polling lean: statewide polls ran too Democratic by 1.17 pts per state sd of white non-college share (Senate + governor 1998-2022, 10 of 13 cycles; not tied to turnout or to the national miss; out of sample Senate log loss -3.8 %) - governors get the same; heating-oil adjustment by state fuel-oil share; appointed incumbents (Husted, Moody) get 0.6 of the incumbency term (12 appointees 2006-22 averaged +6.3 over an open-seat prior); national shock 3.2 x 0.8, the SAME draw as the House, so joint control is coherent
notes.backtests: Live House path, leave-one-year-out (backtest_all live), 15 Sep: 2022 214 (196-231) vs 213 actual, PIT 0.47; 2018 231 (208-258) vs 235, PIT 0.64. 12 dates: Brier 0.0375, actual inside the 10-90 % range every time; the model ran slightly Republican at most dates (mean PIT 0.64)
